content:
nina: Noticing a spike of 1-GPU pods stuck `Pending` in ap-southeast1, mostly in cluster-prod. Feels like AZ stickiness again.
raj: Can you share a few `kubectl describe` lines? :mag:
carmen: quick dump: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase==Pending --namespace=ml` shows about 28 pending, many requesting 1 GPU.
nina: Minimal example:
```
NAME                    STATUS   NODE   REASON
job-infer-9c8d          Pending  <none> InsufficientGPU
spawn-test-6b2          Pending  <none> InsufficientGPU
```
Node labels:
```
node-az-a-07  topology.kubernetes.io/zone=ap-southeast1a  gpu.count=4  taints=gpu-enterprise:NoSchedule
node-az-b-02  topology.kubernetes.io/zone=ap-southeast1b  gpu.count=8  taints=
node-az-c-09  topology.kubernetes.io/zone=ap-southeast1c  gpu.count=0  taints=gpu-realtime:NoSchedule
```
raj: Interesting that b has capacity but a lot of enterprise taints in a so traffic piled into b. SchedulerPolicy includes `preferSameZone: true` for workloads labeled `--affinity=local`.
leo: That `preferSameZone` was intended to keep NVLink-local gangs together. But we didn't scope it by pod size, so tiny 1-GPU jobs are blocked when preferred AZ gets saturated.
sysbot: alert: pending_gpus(ap-southeast1)>20 triggered at 2026-03-21T15:02:18Z.
raj: Proposals:
- quick canary: relax zone affinity for pods with `resources.requests.gpu<=1` in that region only.
- run short defrag: cordon nodes in b temporarily and let scheduler fill a and c where appropriate.
- disable enterprise taint tolerance for non-enterprise pods? no, dangerous.
carmen: I can craft the scheduler patch. But we should be careful: relaxing affinity might spread gang jobs and regress latency for large multi-gpu training jobs.
nina: Agreed. Canary only for pods with label `tiny-gpu=true` and for namespace `ml-staging` first.
leo: Also propose a safer defrag: a controller that only moves non-stateful tiny pods with annotation `migratable=true`, and respects node taints/labels (no touching enterprise nodes).
raj: Timeline suggestion:
- 15:10 apply scheduler policy canary to ap-southeast1
- 15:10-15:25 watch schedule success and p95 latencies for training jobs
- 15:30 run defrag controller for 10m if pending remains >10
- 16:00 evaluate rollback or region expansion
nina: Add a cost guardrail: if cluster-autoscaler triggers >2 new nodes in region, post to #finance-alerts and pause autoscaler.
sysbot: scheduled action: /ops/scheduler-canary/6543210000 at 2026-03-21T15:10Z. Operator: @raj.
carmen: I'll include metrics to watch: `pod_schedule_attempts`, `p95_model-latency`, `node_gpu_utilization_by_zone`, and `pending_gpu_pod_count`.
raj: Also instrument defrag to avoid creating bursty API load; pace evictions at 1/s and only migrate up to 12 pods concurrently.
leo: One more safety net: add admission controller check to prevent tiny-gpu label from being applied to jobs with gang-affinity labels.
nina: Sounds good. If canary shows improvement, we'll promote policy to prod and tune autoscaler to prefer cross-AZ packing for `tiny-gpu=true`.
carmen: Kicking off PR and will paste schedulerpolicy JSON and canary rollout plan here when ready.
sysbot: PR created: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/kube-scheduler/pulls/4897
raj: I'll be on watch during the canary window. Ping here with any anomalies. :eyes:
